With
(Short Term Bail Appl. No.01 of 2026)
Ajay Kulyal --Applicant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand --Respondent
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Mr. R.S. Sammal, learned Senior 
counsel assisted by Ms. Sarita Bisht, learned 
counsel for the applicant. 
2. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned AGA for 
the State.
3. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for 
the complainant. 
4. The short term bail application is 
moved on behalf of the applicant-Ajay 
Kulyal, S/o Jagat Singh Kulyal, who is 
implicated alongwith others in Case Crime 
No.030 of 2026 for the offence punishable 
under Section 109 of BNS, 2023, P.S. Bhimtal, 
District Nainital.
5. The investigation is still going on and 
some of the accused persons are still 
absconding and the condition of the injured 
is critical and as apprised by learned counsel 
for the complainant he is in coma. 
6. In this bail application, the present 
applicant is praying for short term bail on the 
ground that he is pursuing his study in BCA 
in Graphic Era Institute and 5th Semester 
examination are scheduled to be held from 
26th September followed by practical 
examination, therefore he may be granted  short term bail. 
7. There is no objection from the other 
side since the applicant is praying for short 
term bail for the purposes to appear in the 
forth coming examinations. 
8. After considering the submissions as 
above and taking into consideration of forth
coming examination of 5th Semester of BCA, 
this Court is of the view that the applicant 
Ajay Kulyal, S/o Jagat Singh Kulyal deserves 
for short term bail for the period of six 
weeks.
9. Accordingly, I.A. No.01 of 2026 
whereby the applicant is seeking short term 
bail, is allowed. 
10. Let the applicant- Ajay Kulyal be 
released on short term bail for a period of 
six weeks to be reckoned from the date of 
his actual release on his executing a 
personal bond and two sureties of the like 
amount to the satisfaction of the court 
concerned.
11. On expiry of the period of six weeks, 
the applicant shall surrender before the 
Superintendent of the jail concerned.
12. Put up this bail application on the date 
16.10.2026. 
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 15.09.2026

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
UKHC010155052026
BA1/1503/2026
Ajay Kulyal
--Applicant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand
--Respondent
on’ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Piysuh Sammal and Ms. Sarita Bisht
counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Manoj Bhatt, learned Brief Holder for 
the State.
3. Mr. Lalit Sharma and Ms. Anmol 
Sandhu, learned counsel for the complainant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would 
submit that the Coordinate Bench of this 
Court, vide order dated 15.09.2026, granted 
short-term bail to the applicant, taking into 
consideration the fact that he is pursuing a 
B.C.A. course at Graphic Era Institute and 
that his forthcoming fifth-semester 
examination was scheduled to commence on 
26.09.2026.
5. Learned counsel would further submit 
that the present time extension application 
has been filed seeking extension of the short￾term bail for a further period of one month, as 
the applicant is required to appear in the Odd 
Mid-Semester Theory Examination, 2026, 
scheduled to be held from 16.11.2026 to 
23.11.2026, as well as the Odd Mid-Semester  Practical Examinations, scheduled to be held 
from 25.11.2026 to 12.12.2026, as per the 
official examination schedule issued by the 
University.
6. Learned counsel appearing for the 
complainant would oppose the application, 
contending that the applicant is accused of 
having committed a heinous offence and, 
therefore, does not deserve any further 
extension of short-term bail. However, he 
would submit that, in the event the present 
time extension application is allowed, it may 
be made clear that no further application 
seeking extension of short-term bail shall be 
entertained by the Court.
7. Having considered the submissions 
advanced by learned counsel for the parties 
and having regard to the fact that the 
applicant is pursuing his studies and is 
required to appear in the aforesaid 
examinations, this Court is of the view that, in 
the interest of the applicant's academic 
future, the present application deserves to be 
allowed.
8. Accordingly, the time extension 
application is allowed, and the short-term bail 
granted to the applicant vide order dated 
15.09.2026 is extended up to 12.12.2026. The 
applicant shall surrender before the 
competent Court on 14.12.2026. It is, 
however, made clear that no further 
application seeking extension of the short￾term bail shall be entertained.
9. List in due course.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 
 29.10.2026
Mamta
